questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If we had booked the flights earlier, we wouldn't be paying so much now.
If we booked the flights earlier, we wouldn't be paying so much now.
If we had booked the flights earlier, we wouldn't have paid so much now.
If we had booked the flights earlier, we won't pay so much now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If we had booked..., we wouldn't be paying so much now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Overtourism will keep damaging the coastline unless authorities won't limit visitor numbers.
Overtourism will keep damaging the coastline unless authorities limit visitor numbers.
Overtourism will keep damaging the coastline unless that authorities limit visitor numbers.
Overtourism will keep damaging the coastline without authorities limit visitor numbers.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless authorities limit visitor numbers.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several new flight routes has been added this year.
Several new flight routes have added this year.
Several new flight routes have been added this year.
Several new flight routes have being added this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been added this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This overcrowding problem should addressed immediately.
This overcrowding problem should being addressed immediately.
This overcrowding problem should be address immediately.
This overcrowding problem should be addressed immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be addressed immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please keep your passport with you at all times.")
options: The guide told us to keep our passports with us at all times.
The guide told us keep our passports with us at all times.
The guide said us to keep our passports with us at all times.
The guide told us that keep our passports with us at all times.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to keep our passports with us.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should book accommodation in advance.")
options: She suggested to book accommodation in advance.
She suggested booking accommodation in advance.
She suggested me booking accommodation in advance.
She suggested that I booking accommodation in advance.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested booking accommodation in advance.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The agency which she works for it organizes eco-tours.
The agency for that she works organizes eco-tours.
The agency for which she works organizes eco-tours.
The agency she works for which organizes eco-tours.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the agency for which she works.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The report publishing last week revealed a rise in tourist numbers.
The report published last week reveal a rise in tourist numbers.
The report which published last week revealed a rise in tourist numbers.
The report published last week revealed a rise in tourist numbers.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The report published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The airline must have cancelled the flight due to bad weather.
The airline must cancelled the flight due to bad weather.
The airline must have cancel the flight due to bad weather.
The airline must has cancelled the flight due to bad weather.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have cancelled the flight.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The tour operator should acted sooner to warn tourists.
The tour operator should have acted sooner to warn tourists.
The tour operator should have act sooner to warn tourists.
The tour operator should has acted sooner to warn tourists.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: International travel rose significantly over the past decade.
International travel has risen significantly over the past decade.
International travel have risen significantly over the past decade.
International travel have rose significantly over the past decade.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past decade' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'has risen significantly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time we reached the airport, our flight left.
By the time we had reached the airport, our flight left.
By the time we reached the airport, our flight have already left.
By the time we reached the airport, our flight had already left.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'our flight had already left.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Tourism officials are meeting next week to discuss new regulations.
Tourism officials meet next week to discuss new regulations.
Tourism officials will meeting next week to discuss new regulations.
Tourism officials are meet next week to discuss new regulations.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He said he will visit three countries this summer.
He said he would visit three countries this summer.
He said he would visited three countries this summer.
He said he would have visit three countries this summer.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'he said he would visit three countries.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish local authorities take overtourism more seriously.
I wish local authorities have taken overtourism more seriously.
I wish local authorities took overtourism more seriously.
I wish local authorities would take overtourism more seriously as a policy.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish local authorities took overtourism more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish the guide warned us earlier about the closure.
I wish the guide have warned us earlier about the closure.
I wish the guide would have warned us earlier about the closure.
I wish the guide had warned us earlier about the closure.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish the guide had warned us earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had our visas processed by a travel agency.
We had processed our visas by a travel agency.
We had our visas process by a travel agency.
We have our visas processed by a travel agency last year.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had our visas processed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the island had received so many visitors.
Never before had the island received so many visitors.
Never before did the island received so many visitors.
Never before has the island had received so many visitors.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the island received...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The airline is looking the complaint into.
The airline is looking in to the complaint.
The airline is looking into the complaint.
The airline is looking into to the complaint.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the complaint.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What the region urgently needs are better public transport for tourists.
That the region urgently needs is better public transport for tourists.
What the region urgently needs is better public transport for tourists it.
What the region urgently needs is better public transport for tourists.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What the region needs is better public transport.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some resorts protect local wildlife, whereas others harm the ecosystem.
Some resorts protect local wildlife, whereas others harms the ecosystem.
Some resorts protect local wildlife whereas, others harm the ecosystem.
Some resorts protect local wildlife despite others harm the ecosystem.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others harm the ecosystem.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the bad weather, the trip was a success.
In spite of the bad weather, the trip was a success.
Despite of the bad weather, the trip was a success.
In spite of the bad weather, the trip was a success though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the bad weather, the trip was a success.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked overtourism to environmental damage.
The number of studies have linked overtourism to environmental damage.
A number of studies have linked overtourism to environmental damage.
A great number of studies has linked overtourism to environmental damage.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire tour group.
She spoke on behalf for the entire tour group.
She spoke behalf of the entire tour group.
She spoke on behalf of the entire tour group.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the tour group.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The introduction of a tourist tax reduced overcrowding significantly.
The introduce of a tourist tax reduced overcrowding significantly.
The introducing of a tourist tax reduced overcrowding significantly.
The introduction of a tourist tax reduce overcrowding significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'introduce' becomes 'the introduction of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a hotel's cancellation policy?
options: I'm writing to ask you about your cancellation policy, ok?
I am writing to enquire about your cancellation policy.
Just wanted to know about your cancellation policy.
Hey, tell me about your cancellation policy.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a cancelled flight?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about my cancelled flight.
I want to complain about my cancelled flight, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about my cancelled flight.
I am writing to express my concern about my cancelled flight, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The delays at the airport were extreme alarming.
The delays at the airport were extremely alarm.
The delays at the airport were very much alarming.
The delays at the airport were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The resort is affordable. Moreover, it offers free excursions.
The resort is affordable, moreover it offers free excursions.
The resort is affordable. Moreover it offers free excursions.
The resort is affordable moreover, it offers free excursions.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The resort is affordable. Moreover, it offers free excursions.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd recommend this destination, didn't you?
You'd recommend this destination, wouldn't you?
You'd recommend this destination, would you?
You'd recommend this destination, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd recommend..., wouldn't you?'
